result.markdown:
For most small businesses, I'd recommend **Dropbox Sign** for simplicity and predictable costs, or **DocuSign** if you want the most widely recognized e-signature platform.

However, the best choice depends on how many contracts you send and whether you need features beyond collecting signatures.

## Best e-signature software for small businesses

![PandaDoc Review: Sign, Seal, Deliver](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/0MUKV24vOJ8Fy84anuzrEeDfSf0kpDjVQFizvzFH_No27CWsxijbo2OMMlOGpvgS85vZB3wg04yrL3uUEA8HfUdyjeWSSz3aH8VUzmHL1gINYfR2lzt9WJR1seELOV2zEpePqA9WPggyXDEs9xtNtG6ptm3fJ7rmZx4q6N4W7fYpmzjZfQx9dTipSbsTdrj3?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Dropbox Sign**

(Best overall for small businesses)

- Simple to use and easy for clients.
- Templates and signing reminders.
- Unlimited signature requests on paid plans.
- Good Dropbox integration.

Starting around \$15/month with annual billing.

[Visit Dropbox Sign](https://sign.dropbox.com/)

**2\. DocuSign**

(Best for professional credibility)

- Widely recognized by customers and businesses.
- Strong integrations with business software.
- Document tracking and audit trails.
- More advanced agreement workflows.

Starting around \$10–\$15/month for entry-level plans, depending on billing.

[Visit DocuSign](https://www.docusign.com/)

---

![PandaDoc buys Denario for consolidated document and payment workflow offering](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/nMZU-ikvjF7B27p2YRYbwMFVYldny8ofYsWDYYkqTXdGfrk-N9sresjiQS7_N5GL_z3bC2xtBlASA1wbjcPGc7QwN2zoEnDhBBAByuwL6PooRYdhb5Xb7bjGtsls49X_kKuOQ8O8ieH---UeiE5fGOQC1qFIRtUd6uc0-JR89a70cw5k0Vpz1IUhRMFOX01b?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. PandaDoc**

(Best for proposals and contracts)

- Create proposals, quotes and contracts.
- Reusable document templates.
- Electronic signatures and document tracking.
- Sales workflow integrations.

Free tier available; paid plans start around \$19/user/month annually.

[Visit PandaDoc](https://www.pandadoc.com/)

---

![Best e-signature software | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/wmbNwQd5sZcCQM_y8xDHl0CPe7pgdwCT-krxdtJ31tc_1PKqy7PiBHAl_-Gd913WdMSfKG4tvcbm87CrehlVzyh0S_XfsJoy8bGchL0mjaA3hnz0pBJgnLcUXZcQanS1poRpGWtqsda_EXu0W3Y1sz9Tm8p7il83hsR4mOfYqnnCRPXfp1UL4Ot3PT4uhG1W?purpose=fullsize)

## My comparison

| Software | Best use | Main drawback |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Dropbox Sign | Everyday contracts | Fewer advanced workflows |
| DocuSign | Business agreements | Can get expensive |
| PandaDoc | Proposals and sales | More features than some need |
| SignNow | Budget-conscious teams | Annual sending limits |
| Adobe Sign | PDF-heavy businesses | Less focused on signing alone |


## What I'd look for before purchasing

For a small business, prioritize\:

1. Unlimited or sufficient monthly signature requests.
2. Reusable contract templates.
3. Automatic reminders for unsigned contracts.
4. Audit trails and downloadable signed PDFs.
5. Legally valid electronic signatures.
6. Integrations with your existing CRM, accounting or document storage software.

In the US, look for compliance with the ESIGN Act and applicable state electronic-signature laws.
